rows.name: File is PDF-compatible
rows.description: Parses as PDF. Confirmed on all 4 samples.
rows.remediation_text: This file was not saved with PDF compatibility. Ask seps.io to resave from Illustrator with 'Create PDF Compatible File' checked.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 pass

rows.name: Standard layers present
rows.description: Reports the layer structure. Layer names and which layer holds the art both vary legitimately across files and eras (2021-23 files have no Koozie Guides layer; recent files put art on either PASTE ART HERE or Reg Marks & Info). Informational only.
rows.remediation_text: Layer structure differs from the common template. Not a defect.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 pass

rows.name: Artboard contains artwork
rows.description: Each artboard must carry actual separation geometry. Which LAYER it sits on is not a defect - artists paste art onto whichever layer is active, and a finished output file is judged on having art, a filename and swatch names, not on layer hygiene.
rows.remediation_text: This artboard has no artwork on it at all. Send back to seps.io.
rows.validated_against: 31/31 artboards across the 2025-26 corpus carry art. 8/16 of the #22541-#22600 batch carry it on Reg Marks & Info rather than PASTE ART HERE - confirmed by Tyler as normal, not a fault

rows.name: Swatch names follow head-mesh-ink
rows.description: Names match {head}-{mesh}-{ink}. Compound forms are legitimate and carry meaning: TWO head groups with ONE ink = same art burned on two screens (double-hit white, or varying mesh). TWO head groups with TWO inks = one film used for two garment colourways. ONE head group with TWO inks = an INK CHANGE mid-production: the press is stopped, one ink cleaned out and the other loaded. All three are valid - do not fail any of them.
rows.remediation_text: A swatch name does not follow our head-mesh-ink convention. Ask seps.io to rename - our press setup and plate ordering both key off this structure.
rows.validated_against: 11/11 real names pass. 22699 "5-200-Grey 429 & Yellow 121" is an ink change, NOT an error - an earlier draft wrongly failed it. 22591 "1-160&10-160-White&Navy 289" has no spaces around the ampersand and was rejected by the earlier pattern - both spellings are legitimate

rows.name: Registration swatch present
rows.description: The 'All' swatch (DeviceCMYK 1,1,1,1) carries registration marks.
rows.remediation_text: No registration swatch found. Confirm the file was run through Pre-Press Pro - without registration marks the press cannot align the plates.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 present

rows.name: No duplicate head positions
rows.description: Two separations assigned to the same head is a press setup conflict.
rows.remediation_text: Two separations are assigned to the same head position. Ask seps.io to renumber - as delivered this cannot be set up on press.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 pass

rows.name: Underbase on a coarser mesh
rows.description: Underbase runs 160; colours run 200-230.
rows.remediation_text: The underbase is specified on a finer mesh than we normally run. Confirm with the artist - the base usually runs 160 to lay down enough ink.
rows.validated_against: 2/2 underbase files = 160 mesh

rows.name: Underbase identified by name, colour corroborates
rows.description: Name is authoritative: the underbase is the swatch whose ink segment is "Under". Rhodamine Red (229,6,149) is the display proxy but is ALSO a real ink - see 6-230-Rhodamine Red C in 91825 - so display colour alone must never assign the underbase role.
rows.remediation_text: A swatch named as the underbase does not display in Rhodamine Red, or the roles are otherwise unclear. Ask seps.io to confirm which separation is the base before this goes to the floor - note that Rhodamine Red is also a legitimate ink, so the name is what decides.
rows.validated_against: 2/2 agree; 91825 proves colour alone gives a false positive

rows.name: Trap total, where a trap is present
rows.description: Reports the trap sum where trapping exists. The invariant when trapped is choke_pt + spread_pt = 0.75 per shape pair (0.375 pt net), however split: A all choke, B all spread, C any split. This rule does NOT require a trap to exist - absence of trap is frequently correct (see TRAP_AT_NEGATIVE_SPACE). It only reports whether the trapping that IS present sums correctly.
rows.remediation_text: A trapped shape does not sum to 0.75pt. Choke and spread may be split any way that totals 0.75 - ask seps.io for the missing amount, not for a particular technique.
rows.validated_against: A: 11/11 (22499), 7/7 (22880). B: 161/161 (91825). C: 8/8 (21825) at 0.25 spread + 0.50 choke = 0.75, bbox delta 0.0pt after removing the planted 1pt offset

rows.name: Mixed trap techniques sum correctly
rows.description: SUPERSEDED as a defect check. Mixing choke and spread within one file - and within one shape - is legitimate; what matters is that each shape totals 0.75pt. Retained only to surface the mix so a reviewer knows what they are looking at.
rows.remediation_text: This file mixes choke and spread. That is allowed when each shape totals 0.75pt - check the trap total rather than the technique.
rows.validated_against: 21825 mixes all three techniques and every shape that totals 0.75 is correct

rows.name: Choke does not erase fine base detail
rows.description: Simulate a 0.375pt erosion of the underbase geometry. If shapes fragment or vanish, a choke destroys base under fine detail - the top colour then prints straight onto the garment there and reads duller than the same ink elsewhere. Spread-on-colour must be used instead.
rows.remediation_text: This artwork has base detail too fine to choke - shapes fragment or disappear at 0.375pt. Ask seps.io to spread the colour instead of choking the base. If the base is choked away under small detail, the colour prints directly on the garment there and will look duller than the same ink elsewhere in the print.
rows.validated_against: DISABLED pending recalibration. The erosion-topology prediction matched seps.io's technique choice on 3/3 files during phase 0, but the rebuilt detector reports 2 vanishing shapes on 22499 - a file Tyler confirmed good and correctly choked. The metric is sensitive to render dpi, kernel shape and whether it runs on authored or composited geometry; it is not shipping until those are pinned down.

rows.name: Underbase artwork aligns with the colour artwork
rows.description: Match art-layer shapes across artboards by size, then take the median translation between them. A uniform non-zero offset means one artboard has been nudged - the plates will not register on press even though the artboards and registration marks line up perfectly.
rows.remediation_text: The underbase artwork is shifted relative to the colour artwork - the plates will not register on press. The registration marks still line up, so this will not be caught by eye at the press. Ask seps.io to realign the artboards and resend.
rows.validated_against: planted-error test: 21825 nudged one artboard by a single arrow click -> detected exactly 1.000pt dx across 126/126 shapes. 22499 0.000 (48/48), 22880 0.000 (54/54), 91825 0.000 (355/365)

rows.name: Fill and stroke on one object use the same ink
rows.description: A path filled in one separation and stroked in another is unusual at Mint and changes how the object interacts with the underbase - the base is built from the fill, so a stroke in a different ink extends past it untrapped.
rows.remediation_text: An object is filled in one ink and stroked in another. Confirm this is intended - the underbase is built from the fill, so the stroke ink will extend past the base with no trap. Also check the stroke weight.
rows.validated_against: caught 22563 planted defect: 2 paths filled 5-230-Blue 286 C, stroked 6-230-Gray 432 at 0.1pt

rows.name: Based colour abutting negative space must be trapped
rows.tolerance: {"note": "three-state: below 70 untrapped = fail, 70-85 untrapped = flag, above 85 = pass"}
rows.description: A based colour needs a trap only where its perimeter meets negative space (bare garment). Where the colour is bounded by another ink - typically a white or a colour that is itself knocked out of the underbase - it sits snugly inside that ink and needs no choke. Measured as the fraction of each colorant's perimeter adjacent to another ink. White is exempt: it is the bounding ink and needs no choke over base.
rows.remediation_text: A colour on the underbase meets bare garment at its edge with no trap. Ask seps.io for the standard 0.75pt trap. Shapes fully enclosed by a knocked-out colour do not need one - a minimal choke there is optional habit, not a requirement.
rows.validated_against: 13 colorant measurements at 200dpi. Untrapped files (22583 B/F, 22563 F, 22560 B/RS) non-white inks: 76.2-93.4% abutting. Trapped files (22599 B, 22596 B, 22586 F): 0.0-56.0%. Clean separation, no overlap. Also caught the 21797 planted defect

rows.name: No choke where white prints on base
rows.description: Underbase beneath white takes no stroke.
rows.remediation_text: A choke has been applied to base beneath white ink. White on white needs no choke - confirm with seps.io, though this is cosmetic rather than a press problem.
rows.validated_against: 47 white fills -> 0 (22880); 43 white fills -> 0 strokes (91825)

rows.name: Inks overlap only in a trap band
rows.description: NEEDS TUNING. Rasterise each ink plate and measure the maximum inscribed width of every pairwise overlap. A trap band is thin; a solid overlap means one ink is sitting under another unexpectedly - usually misregistration within a single artboard, which ARTWORK_IN_REGISTER cannot see.
rows.remediation_text: Two inks overlap by more than a trap band - one colour appears to be sitting underneath another. Check registration and layering against the approved proof before this goes to the floor.
rows.validated_against: detects 22875 planted defect (Brown 2.40pt vs blues). Good files: 22834 max 1.07pt, 91825 max 1.36pt at 0.0% area. Threshold 2.0pt separates on 9 files - NOT well calibrated, needs more corpus

rows.name: Swatch label block matches the artwork
rows.description: Pre-Press Pro writes the swatch list as LIVE text on the Reg Marks & Info layer. That block is a machine-readable manifest of intended inks. Extract it and cross-check against (a) the separations declared in /ColorSpace and (b) the separations actually painted. Three independent views of the same list.
rows.remediation_text: The swatch label block on the file does not match the artwork. Check which list is right before releasing - the label is what the press operator reads.
rows.validated_against: 22554: label lists 5 inks including 5-230-Gold 110 C; /ColorSpace declares all 5; only 4 are painted. Text extraction verified working via ToUnicode maps

rows.name: Ink change noted for production
rows.description: A swatch with ONE head group and TWO ink names signals an ink change mid-run: the press stops, one ink is cleaned out and the other loaded. Not a defect - surface it so scheduling and the press know.
rows.remediation_text: This job includes an ink change on one head - the press will stop, clean and reload mid-run. Make sure production scheduling accounts for it.
rows.validated_against: 22699 "5-200-Grey 429 & Yellow 121" - confirmed by Tyler as an ink change

rows.name: Stray sub-spec strokes look like trim residue
rows.description: Zero-ink strokes well under the 0.75pt trap spec, on a job with no trapping need, are usually residue left by an Illustrator trim operation. Often harmless, occasionally left deliberately because removing them changes the look. A judgement call, never an automatic reject.
rows.remediation_text: Stray zero-ink strokes below trap spec - most likely residue from an Illustrator trim. Usually harmless, but check whether removing them changes the look before releasing.
rows.validated_against: 18496: 14 zero-ink strokes at 0.25pt on a white-only job - confirmed as trim residue

rows.name: Gradient blend technique present
rows.description: Gradients painted with sh shading operators, where artboards carry different inks that blend at the seam. One colour is deliberately run further beneath the other so the transition is smooth without needing impeccable registration. A recognised technique - surface it, do not fail it.
rows.remediation_text: Gradient blending across artboards is a deliberate technique for a smooth transition. Not a fault - confirm layering with the press operator and do not auto-release.
rows.validated_against: 22617: 23 sh ops per artboard, Separation-based shadings in Yellow 108/White (AB0) and Orange 158/Blue 7688/Cool Gray 11 (AB1) - confirmed as a deliberate blend technique

rows.name: Base exists under every colour that needs one
rows.expected: {"partial_below_pct": 15, "partial_above_pct": 85, "note": "an ink between these two is only partly based, which prints two shades"}
rows.description: Counts colour shapes requiring a base against base copies found.
rows.remediation_text: The number of underbase shapes does not match the number of colour shapes needing a base. Something was missed - send back to seps.io with the shape count.

rows.name: Underbase present on dark garments
rows.description: Dark garment jobs need a base under every non-black ink. Black prints direct.
rows.remediation_text: This is a dark garment with no underbase separation. Send back to seps.io - the colours will not opacity up without one.
rows.validated_against: confirmed by Tyler: black on dark takes no base

rows.name: No underbase on light garments
rows.description: A base on a white garment is a wasted screen.
rows.remediation_text: An underbase is present on a light garment. Confirm with the artist - if it is not needed, ask seps.io to remove it and save a screen.
rows.validated_against: untested - no light-garment sample

rows.name: Every art object uses a spot separation
rows.description: Generalises the old RGB check. Every painted object on the art layer must use a /Separation (or /DeviceN of separations). ICCBased, DeviceCMYK, DeviceRGB and DeviceGray fills are unconverted art and will not separate - the zero-ink knockout fill is the only legitimate exception.
rows.remediation_text: An object is painted in a colour space that is not one of our spot separations - it will not separate to a plate. Ask seps.io to convert it to the correct named spot swatch, or remove it.
rows.validated_against: caught 22829 planted defect: ICCBased N=4 fill at C0.024 M0.663 Y0.690 K0 (orange)

rows.name: No stray CMYK plates
rows.description: Process plates in a spot job usually mean an unconverted object.
rows.remediation_text: Process (CMYK) plates carry ink in a spot-colour job. Ask seps.io whether this is intentional simulated process or a conversion that was missed.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 pass

rows.name: Every declared separation carries artwork
rows.description: Compare the separations DECLARED in /ColorSpace against the separations actually painted (fills, strokes AND sh shadings). A declared colorant with no marks is a screen burned for nothing, and usually means a colour was dropped from the art but left in the swatch list.
rows.remediation_text: A separation is declared in the swatches but has no artwork on any artboard. Either a colour was dropped from the design and left in the swatch list, or artwork is missing. Confirm the intended colour count with the order before burning screens.
rows.validated_against: caught 22554 planted defect: 5-230-Gold 110 C declared and labelled, zero marks

rows.name: All artwork text outlined
rows.description: Live text must be outlined. Neither the layer nor the ink discriminates the info block from artwork: art legitimately sits on the Reg Marks layer, and the swatch labels are painted in each ink. POSITION does - Pre-Press Pro sets the filename and label block in the margin strip above the artwork, so a text run whose origin falls inside the art bounding box is artwork text wherever it lives.
rows.remediation_text: Live text is sitting on the artwork. Ask seps.io to outline it - type reflows on a machine without the font. Text in the margin strip is the filename and swatch labels and is expected to stay live.
rows.validated_against: 55 files: exactly 1 run in 1 file (22560 B) lands inside the art. Two earlier versions of this rule were withdrawn - filtering by layer fired on every file whose art sits on the marks layer, and filtering by ink fired on the swatch labels, which are painted in their own ink by design

rows.name: Marks layer text is expected
rows.description: Informational. Live text on Reg Marks & Info is the script's own output, not a defect.
rows.remediation_text: No file info or swatch labels found on the marks layer. The file may not have been run through Pre-Press Pro - confirm before release.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 have 2-8 live text ops

rows.name: Placed images at least 300 dpi
rows.description: Effective resolution at placed size.
rows.remediation_text: A placed image is below 300 dpi at its placed size. Check the plate preview - if the halftone looks soft, request higher-resolution art from the customer.
rows.validated_against: UNTESTED - no sample has a raster

rows.name: Placed images above hard floor
rows.description: Below 200 dpi is not printable at any size we run.
rows.remediation_text: A placed image is below 200 dpi at placed size and will visibly pixelate. Request higher-resolution source art before this goes to the floor.
rows.validated_against: UNTESTED - no sample has a raster

rows.name: Placed images not RGB
rows.description: Checked specifically on rasters.
rows.remediation_text: A placed image is still in RGB. Ask seps.io to convert it into the separation.
rows.validated_against: UNTESTED - no sample has a raster

rows.name: No zero-width strokes
rows.description: A 0pt stroke will not hold on press.
rows.remediation_text: Zero-width (hairline) strokes found. Ask seps.io to set a real stroke weight - hairlines drop out or print inconsistently.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 pass

rows.name: Minimum stroke weight
rows.description: Below the minimum will not hold at our mesh counts.
rows.remediation_text: Strokes thinner than 0.25pt found. These may not hold on press. Confirm with the artist or ask seps.io to thicken.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 pass

rows.name: Plate count matches ordered colours
rows.description: Unique colorants across ALL artboards, minus 'All'.
rows.remediation_text: The separation count does not match the colour count on the order. Either the order is wrong or seps.io added or merged a colour - resolve before screens are burned, this is a costing issue.
rows.validated_against: 4/4 match stated colour counts

rows.name: Artboards share trim size and origin
rows.description: Geometry check only — artboards must be the same size and origin so plates overlay. This does NOT verify that the artwork aligns; see ARTWORK_IN_REGISTER.
rows.remediation_text: The artboards in this file are not the same size or origin. Ask seps.io to resave with matching artboards - as delivered the separations cannot be overlaid.
rows.validated_against: 2/2 multi-artboard files pass

rows.name: Print size within location preset
rows.description: Artwork bounds on the art layer against the location preset max.
rows.remediation_text: Artwork is larger than our preset maximum for this print location. Check against the approved proof - either the proof was approved at this size, or seps.io scaled it.
rows.validated_against: untested - needs presets loaded

rows.name: Opacity below 100% present
rows.description: Any fill or group below 100% opacity is converted to halftones by the RIP when the plate is output. This is a deliberate technique, not a fault - like gradient blending, it signals a file that needs precise layering at press. Report it so the press operator knows, and route it out of any automated generator.
rows.remediation_text: This file uses opacity below 100%, which halftones at RIP. Intentional special handling - confirm layering with the press operator; do not auto-release.
rows.validated_against: 1 of 24 files. 22541 B REVISED carries six alpha values (0.2, 0.25, 0.37, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5) plus one soft mask; the other 23 files have none. No blend modes anywhere in the corpus - alpha alone is the signal

rows.name: Mesh tally for the screen department
rows.description: Counts screens per mesh from the swatch names. Not a pass/fail check - this is the forecast input the screen room needs (e.g. 160mesh-2, 230mesh-3).
rows.validated_against: parses 16/17 historical names; '1-110 Under' uses a space delimiter and is handled
